messages.content: You can call send_email to compose and send messages. Always confirm critical fields before sending.
Send an email to alice@example.com thanking her for yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM.

function.name: send_email
function.description: Compose and send an email message.

message.content:
<think>The user wants me to send an email to alice@example.com thanking her for yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM. I need to use the send_email function with the appropriate parameters.

Let me compose the email:
- to: ["alice@example.com"]
- subject: Something like "Thank You for Yesterday's Meeting" or "Follow-up from Our Meeting"
- body: A thank you message mentioning yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM

I should craft a professional but warm email.
</think>

function.name: send_email
function.arguments:
{"to": ["alice@example.com"], "subject": "Thank You for Yesterday's Meeting - Follow-up", "body": "Hi Alice,

Thank you for taking the time to meet with me yesterday. I really appreciated the discussion and found your insights valuable.

I would love to continue our conversation. Would you be available for a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM? Please let me know if that time works for you or if you have another preferred time.

Looking forward to hearing from you.

Best regards"}
